page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance based on KVM virtualization and the x86_64 architecture. The server is driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 16 dedicated vCPUs sourced from 8 physical execution cores with hyperthreading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The hardware architecture features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a 35 MB L3 cache pool, alongside instruction set support for AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES-NI, and BMI2. Hardware acceleration is absent, with zero GPUs bundled. Local instance storage is not included, requiring external block storage for persistent data, while networking is configured with a baseline throughput of 5 Gbps without bundled public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reflect a distinct split between single-threaded execution and parallel multi-threaded throughput. Multi-threaded evaluations position the instance firmly in the middle 50% performance bracket, recording 11,807.11 on stress-ng multi-core tests, 6,333.0 on Geekbench multi-core, and 13,076.83 on PassMark CPU score. Software compilation via Clang achieves 10,468.0, and static web serving throughput measures 9.93 GB/sec. Conversely, single-core processing demonstrates lower efficiency, scoring 1,107.09 in stress-ng and 1,025.0 in Geekbench single-core, alongside lower-tier single-threaded gzip compression at 19.31 GB/sec. In-memory throughput is stable, yielding 61.39 GB/sec read and 55.37 GB/sec write on uncached 256 MB blocks, with Redis SET operations sustaining 11.41 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the compute-dense allocation minimizes resource overhead by avoiding bundled local NVMe storage and high memory overheads. This structure delivers cost-effective execution for parallel tasks that fully saturate 16 threads without consuming excessive memory per worker. The primary hardware tradeoffs include modest single-thread clock rates, the absence of local storage I/O capabilities, and restricted per-core memory capacity that limits large-scale dataset caching or heavy memory-bound analytics.

Workload suitability centers on parallelized compute tasks that can operate efficiently within a 32 GB footprint. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.4xlarge is appropriate for software build automation and Clang compilations, multi-threaded batch decompression, Redis key-value caching clusters, static web serving nodes, and moderate continuous integration pipelines.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at 2.5 GHz, the instance incorporates instruction sets including AVX-512 and BMI2. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage configurations. Baseline network throughput is rated at 5 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the platform demonstrates mid-tier multi-core computing metrics across PassMark CPU and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression tests, whereas single-core processing and compression workloads show lower relative throughput. Its hardware balance provides cost efficiency for multi-threaded computational tasks that do not require heavy per-core memory footprints or local disk I/O. Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.4xlarge fits workloads such as multi-threaded batch processing, Clang software compilation, static web serving, and caching tiers like Redis.
